usageNotes: Reads the systemd journal (journald) for a specific cluster node, returning an array of log line strings. Requires the `Sys.Syslog` privilege on `/nodes/{node}`, so API tokens must be granted that privilege explicitly. Use cursor-based pagination (`startcursor`/`endcursor`) for efficient incremental reads; time-range filters (`since`/`until`) accept UNIX epoch integers — note that `since` conflicts with `startcursor` and `until` conflicts with `endcursor`, so only one pagination strategy can be used per request.

examples.summary: Fetch the last 100 journal entries from node pve1

tips: Use `lastentries` for a quick tail-style view; omit all filters to retrieve the full journal (can be very large on busy nodes).
Cursor values are opaque strings returned in prior responses; store them to implement reliable forward pagination without duplicates.
Time-range (`since`/`until`) and cursor (`startcursor`/`endcursor`) filters are mutually exclusive pairs — mixing them will result in an API error.
The node must be online and reachable by the Proxmox API; offline nodes will return an error rather than cached logs.
